memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'In this Year of Jubilee everyone is to return to their own property.
If you sell land to any of your own people or buy land from them, do not
take advantage of each other'" - Lev 25:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Jubilee had a very practical effect on daily business. Because land
returned to its original family every fifty years, no sale was truly
permanent. So God gave a simple command: do not take advantage of each
other.

Every transaction in Israel was to be conducted in the awareness that God
was watching and that the land ultimately belonged to Him. That
changed how people bought and sold.

Dear friend, faith is meant to reach into our commerce, not just our
church attendance. How we price things, how we negotiate, whether we
exploit someone's desperation or ignorance — these are spiritual matters.

Proverbs says the LORD detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights
find favour with Him (Prov 11:1). Paul instructs believers not to wrong or
take advantage of a brother in business, because the Lord will punish such
things (1 Thess 4:6).

It is possible to sing on Sunday and cheat on Monday, and to feel no
tension between the two. God allows no such split. The same Lord rules the
sanctuary and the marketplace.

Is there any dealing in your life — at work, in a sale, in a negotiation —
that would not survive God's gaze? Bring your business under His lordship
today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would my business dealings survive God's gaze?
2. Have I ever taken advantage of someone's weakness or need?
3. How can I bring more integrity into my work this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You see every transaction I make. Give me honesty in my dealings
and keep me from ever exploiting another person for gain. Amen.
